title: Power Up Consumption: Impact of Electric Vehicle Infrastructure on Household Finance
abstract: arXiv:2609.19034v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: To achieve carbon neutrality, electrifying vehicles in a cleaner electricity grid has become a key pathway for global cities. While extensive research has examined the environmental benefits of electric vehicles (EVs), their financial impacts remain underexplored. Using Singapore-a smart city-state - as a social laboratory, we combine high-resolution data on the geographic distribution of EV chargers with nearly 1 million individual-level monthly expenditure records from a major commercial bank and about 65,000 housing transaction records, spanning January 2019 to March 2021. Our results show that proximity to charging stations during the initial phase of EV infrastructure rollout significantly increases household consumption by 1-3%. This effect is driven primarily by public housing residents, who are generally more financially constrained than their private housing counterparts. translated_title: 充电赋能消费：电动汽车基础设施对家庭财务的影响
translated_abstract: 为实现碳中和，在更清洁的电网中推动车辆电气化已成为全球城市的关键路径。尽管已有大量研究考察了电动汽车（EV）的环境效益，但其对家庭财务的影响仍未得到充分探索。我们以新加坡这一智慧城市国家作为“社会实验室”，将电动汽车充电桩地理分布的高分辨率数据、来自一家主要商业银行的近100万条个人月度消费记录，以及约6.5万条住房交易记录相结合，数据时间跨度为2019年1月至2021年3月。研究结果表明，在电动汽车基础设施推广的初期阶段，靠近充电站会使家庭消费显著增加1-3%。这一效应主要由公共住房居民驱动，他们通常比私人住房居民面临更强的财务约束。我们识别了这一消费增长背后的三个渠道。
tldr: 研究发现，在新加坡电动汽车基础设施推广初期，居住在充电站附近的家庭消费显著增加1-3%，且该效应主要由财务约束更强的公共住房居民所驱动。
en_tdlr: Proximity to EV charging stations significantly increases household consumption by 1-3% during the initial EV infrastructure rollout in Singapore, with the effect driven primarily by financially constrained public housing residents.
